identity.title: Lottery Prior: Randomized Neural Compression for Zero-Shot Inverse Problems

problem.claim: Recover a clean signal from a single degraded observation without external training data in zero-shot inverse problems.

gap.claim: The abstract challenges the common belief that high-quality zero-shot restoration requires highly complex models.

contributions.claim: Lottery Prior uses random-network architectural priors, compression-based regularization, and randomness-induced implicit priors for ensemble refinement.
The paper derives non-asymptotic error bounds for compression-based maximum-likelihood inverse solvers and characterizes rate–distortion constraints as implicit regularizers.

stated_novelty.claim: A compression-based inverse solver that exploits randomized neural architectures to induce a family of implicit priors and support ensemble-based refinement.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report state-of-the-art results on denoising, noisy super-resolution, and inpainting, using significantly fewer effective parameters.
The authors report that a lightweight network with entropy and complexity regularization is sufficient for high-quality restoration in their compression-based formulation.

narrative_sequence.summary: Defines zero-shot inverse problems as single-observation recovery without external training data.
Argues that lightweight networks can provide high-quality restoration when paired with entropy and complexity regularization.
Introduces Lottery Prior, combining random-network architectural priors with randomness-induced implicit priors and ensemble refinement.
Derives non-asymptotic error bounds and interprets rate–distortion constraints as implicit regularization.
Reports state-of-the-art performance across three inverse-problem settings with fewer effective parameters.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a compression-based solver, randomized architectural priors, and error bounds explaining rate–distortion regularization.

lessons.interpretation: A method claim becomes more interpretable when its design mechanism and a formal account of the relevant constraint are presented together.
lessons.application: When proposing a regularized inverse solver, connect each design component to a stated mechanism and, where possible, a bound or characterization of its effect.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when the method has no tractable formalization or when theoretical assumptions do not match the intended operating regime.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, quantitative metrics, baselines, or the conditions behind the state-of-the-art comparison.
The assumptions, constants, and practical implications of the reported error bounds are not given.
The abstract does not quantify the parameter reduction or define effective parameters.
